TIP_EPOCH_DESC:
An epoch means training the entire dataset once from start to finish.When the data is trained once, it is counted as 1 epoch. Increasing the number of epochs allows the model to learn repeatedly and can improve accuracy, but too many epochs may cause the model to memorize the data and reduce its ability to make proper judgments.

※ Epochs can only be set as whole numbers, such as 1, 2, or 3.
TIP_BATCH_DESC:
Batch size refers to the number of data samples used for training at one time. For example, if the batch size is 5, the entire dataset is divided into groups of 5 for training. A larger batch size can reduce training time by processing more data at once, but it may lower accuracy. On the other hand, a smaller batch size can improve accuracy but may take longer to train.

※ Batch size can only be set as whole numbers, such as 1, 2, or 3.
TIP_LEARNING_RATE_DESC:
The learning rate is a value that controls how fast the model learns. A higher learning rate makes the model learn faster, while a lower learning rate makes it learn more slowly. If the learning rate is too high, accuracy may decrease.

※ The learning rate can be set to a value greater than 0 and up to 1.
TIP_VALIDATION_RATE_TITLE: What is validation data rate(Validation data rate)?
TIP_VALIDATION_RATE_DESC:
It refers to the proportion of validation data within the entire dataset. Validation data is not used for training, but for checking the results after training. If the validation data rate is too high, there may not be enough training data, and if it is too low, the validation may not be sufficient.

※ The validation data rate can be set to a value between 0 and 1.
TIP_TRAIN_ACC_DESC:
You cannot accurately measure performance by testing only on problems you have studied.
That is why the data is divided into training data and validation data.
Training accuracy shows how well the model fits the training data.
If the model answers 90 out of 100 questions correctly, the training accuracy is 0.9 (90/100).
If the model perfectly fits the training data, the value becomes 1.
The lower the correct answer rate, the lower the value.
TIP_VALUE_ACC_DESC:
To properly evaluate performance, you need to test the model on problems it has not seen before.
That is why validation data is not used during training, but only to check results after training.
Validation accuracy shows how well the model predicts the validation data.
If the model answers 80 out of 100 questions correctly, the validation accuracy is 0.8 (80/100).
A higher value means the model can make better judgments on new problems.
TIP_LOSS_DESC:
Loss is a value that shows how different the model’s predictions are from the correct answers.
If the prediction is perfect, the loss is 0.
The more incorrect the prediction, the larger the loss value becomes.
During training, the model continuously adjusts itself to reduce this loss.
Therefore, a smaller loss means the model’s predictions are improving.
TIP_VALUE_LOSS_DESC:
Validation loss shows how different the model’s predictions are from the correct answers when using validation data.
Because validation data is not used for training, it helps evaluate how well the model understands new problems.
A lower validation loss means the model is making better predictions.
